extracted.intended_audience: mystery writers, publishing industry professionals, and readers of literary-award news
extracted.subtask_description: A press-release style announcement listing the 2025 Edgar Allan Poe Award winners and related special awards, noting eligibility year and the organizers' commitment to fair/diverse judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (publication/production year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honoring the best in mystery fiction, nonfiction and television published or produced in 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement explicitly limits consideration to works published or produced in 2024 (i.e., the 2025 awards honor 2024 output).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / Standard — 'distinguished work'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edgar Awards ... are presented to authors of distinguished work in various categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners are selected on the basis of being 'distinguished' within their category; the page does not further define 'distinguished' but uses it as the overarching quality standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging principle — diversity and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Mystery Writers of America would like to emphasize our commitment to diversity and fairness in the judging of the Edgar Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization states judges are selected from every region, from every sub-category of the genre, and from every demographic to ensure fairness and impartiality; this is presented as a process standard for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST NOVEL
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST NOVEL — (winner listed: The In Crowd by Charlotte Vassell).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes a stand-alone novel-length work of mystery fiction; the announcement lists winner and publisher as exemplars.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST FIRST NOVEL BY AN AMERICAN AUTHOR
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST FIRST NOVEL BY AN AMERICAN AUTHOR — (winner listed: Holy City by Henry Wise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category targets debut novels by U.S. authors; winner and publisher are provided as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST PAPERBACK ORIGINAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST PAPERBACK ORIGINAL — (winner listed: The Paris Widow by Kimberly Belle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes original works first published as paperbacks rather than hardcover.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST FACT CRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST FACT CRIME — (winner listed: The Infernal Machine: A True Story of Dynamite, Terror, and the Rise of the Modern Detective by Steven Johnson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category covers nonfiction true-crime works; example winner included.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST CRITICAL/BIOGRAPHICAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST CRITICAL/BIOGRAPHICAL — (winner listed: James Sallis: A Companion to the Mystery Fiction by Nathan Ashman).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes critical studies or biographies related to the mystery field.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST SHORT STORY
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST SHORT STORY — (winner listed: 'Eat My Moose,' Conjunctions: 82, Works & Days by Erika Krouse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes short-form fiction entries (magazine/anthology stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST JUVENILE
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST JUVENILE — (winner listed: Mysteries of Trash and Treasure: The Stolen Key by Margaret Peterson Haddix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes mystery works targeted to juvenile readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST YOUNG ADULT
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST YOUNG ADULT — (winner listed: 49 Miles Alone by Natalie D. Richards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes mystery works targeted to young adult readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: BEST TELEVISION EPISODE TELEPLAY
rubrics_metrics.description: Category: BEST TELEVISION EPISODE TELEPLAY — (winner listed: 'Episode One' – Monsieur Spade, Written by Tom Fontana & Scott Frank (AMC)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category recognizes teleplay writing for television episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROBERT L. FISH MEMORIAL AWARD
rubrics_metrics.description: ROBERT L. FISH MEMORIAL AWARD — Endowed by the family of Robert L. Fish. (winner listed: 'The Jews on Elm Street,' Ellery Queen’s Mystery Magazine, September-October 2024 by Anna Stolley Persky).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A named memorial award listed among other category awards; page does not provide selection criteria beyond the award name and endowment note.

rubrics_metrics.name: THE SIMON & SCHUSTER MARY HIGGINS CLARK AWARD
rubrics_metrics.description: THE SIMON & SCHUSTER MARY HIGGINS CLARK AWARD — Presented on behalf of Simon & Schuster. (winner listed: The Mystery Writer by Sulari Gentill).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A publisher-sponsored named award; specific criteria not described on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: THE G.P. PUTNAM’S SONS SUE GRAFTON MEMORIAL AWARD
rubrics_metrics.description: THE G.P. PUTNAM’S SONS SUE GRAFTON MEMORIAL AWARD — Presented on behalf of G.P. Putnam’s Sons. (winner listed: The Comfort of Ghosts by Jacqueline Winspear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named memorial award; page gives sponsor and winner but no detailed eligibility beyond being a recognized entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: THE LILIAN JACKSON BRAUN MEMORIAL AWARD
rubrics_metrics.description: THE LILIAN JACKSON BRAUN MEMORIAL AWARD — Endowed by the estate of Lilian Jackson Braun. (winner listed: The Murders in Great Diddling by Katarina Bivald).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named memorial award with endowment note; no additional selection criteria provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRAND MASTER (special award)
rubrics_metrics.description: GRAND MASTER — (previously announced winners: Laura Lippman; John Sandford).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lifetime-achievement style honor (implied by 'Grand Master'); the page lists recipients but does not fully define criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAVEN AWARD (special award)
rubrics_metrics.description: RAVEN AWARD — (previously announced winner: Face in a Book Bookstore, El Dorado Hills, CA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A special award recognizing non-writing contributions to the mystery field (implied by recipient being a bookstore); exact criteria not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: ELLERY QUEEN AWARD (special award)
rubrics_metrics.description: ELLERY QUEEN AWARD — (previously announced winner: Peter Wolverton, St. Martin’s Press).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A special award recognizing contributions to mystery publishing/industry; page lists recipient without specifying selection criteria.
